clue.text: Gun that's very good with many rounds

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

indicators.note: rounds means the word for many is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: A gun that is excellent and holds plenty of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is one kind of firearm, so a pistol is a gun.

clue.text: Dad's on trial unfairly? Just a bit

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: unfairly suggests something not done straight, so the letters of trial are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad faces an unjust trial and is only somewhat guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfairly' turns TRIAL into RTIAL, below PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means incomplete, covering only some, so just a bit.

clue.text: Cook eats roast mutton for starter

indicators.note: to roast is to cook, but here it is an instruction to work over the letters of eats
the starter is the first item, so the first letter of mutton is taken

explanation.surface: A chef eats roast mutton as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roast' rearranges EATS into STEA, followed by M.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a way of cooking food over boiling water.

clue.text: Natural produce I can grow, for the most part

indicators.note: to produce is to make, so the letters given are made into a new word
for the most part means most of the word grow is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A grower boasts of the chemical-free vegetables they can raise, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: GROW loses its W; 'produce' rearranges I CAN GRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic food is grown without artificial chemicals, so natural.

clue.text: Judge's terse order? He must be joking!

indicators.note: to order something is to arrange it, so the letters of terse are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge curtly calls for order in court, and someone exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like the judge's call for silence in court; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A court fool's whole job was making jokes, so he is someone who must be joking.

clue.text: Conclusion of election: extremists' date in government

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outside letters, so the first and last of election

explanation.surface: A polling report: radical parties have their moment in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusion of election' tempts as one phrase; only 'Conclusion' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part, a conclusion.

clue.text: Type of ship used by the Krays' gang?

definitions.meaning: the Krays were twin brothers who ran a gang of London criminals in the 1960s

explanation.surface: A kind of boat used by the Kray brothers' criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by two propellers, and the crew of the notorious London gangster twins.

clue.text: They get fired up to score wildly, nothing less over the weekend

indicators.note: over means the letters wrap over and around the end of week
wildly means the letters of to score are thrown about into a new order
less means the letter for nothing is taken away from those letters

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
the end of the word week is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fans get worked up to score frantically, failing to score at all over the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' and 'less' make ROCETS from TO SCORE minus O; 'over' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets are fireworks or missiles, launched by being fired up into the sky.

clue.text: Dance illumination incorporates new atmospheric effect

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: incorporates means takes in, so the letter for new goes inside the word for illumination

parts.note: lighting is illumination

explanation.surface: Dance-floor lights with a novel atmospheric effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' puts N into LIGHTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare glowing sphere seen in thunderstorms, an electrical phenomenon of the atmosphere.

clue.text: Frank Zappa and Elvis overtures dropped from set

indicators.note: dropped from means those opening letters are taken out of the word for set

parts.note: to set is to harden or freeze, as a liquid does

indicators.note: overtures are openings, so the first letters of Zappa and Elvis are taken

explanation.surface: Musicians Frank Zappa and Elvis Presley have their opening numbers cut from a gig's set list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like Zappa's first name but is the definition. Z and E come out of FREEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and free both describe speech that is open and unrestrained.

clue.text: Family member needing car fixed

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative needs their car repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a relative, so a family member.

clue.text: Hired individual to maybe assassinate national leaders?

definitions.text: Hired individual to maybe assassinate national leaders?

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so the first letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to kill heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'national leaders' reads as presidents, but 'leaders' picks the first letter of each of the six words before it, and those words also define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer is paid to murder, which is exactly a hired assassin.

clue.text: Assistant referees can be poets

definitions.meaning: officials on the touchline who flag offside and throw-ins
a poet is cryptically a man of lines, one who writes verses

explanation.surface: Officials who help the referee may also write verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Football assistant referees were formerly called by this name, and poets deal in lines of verse.

clue.text: Close to wedding, girl's mate ignores a weakness in the ring

indicators.note: close means end, so the last letter of wedding is taken

parts.note: lass is a girl

indicators.note: ignores means the letter a is left out of the word for mate

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate)

explanation.surface: As the wedding ends, a girl's partner misses something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests the wedding ring but is the boxing ring. CHINA loses A to give CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer who is easily knocked out is said to have this, a vulnerability in the boxing ring.

clue.text: Persevere? I'd sooner go crazy drinking lager top

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the jumbled letters take in the letter from lager
going crazy means losing order, so the letters of I'd sooner are rearranged
the top of a word is its first letter, here that of lager

explanation.surface: Someone would sooner go mad than stop drinking the best lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go crazy' rearranges I'D SOONER, with L placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly despite difficulty is a phrase meaning persevere.

clue.text: Vessels go south after bow has been removed

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so the first letter of the word for go is dropped

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Ships head south once their front end is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'bow' suggest ships; vessels are containers here, and the bow is just the front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are containers, such as for ashes or tea, so they are vessels.

clue.text: Artist's face, one shifting to one side

indicators.note: shifting to one side means the letter for one moves along to a different place in the word for face

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter's face, one eye drifting sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving I in DIAL gives DALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Student union card revoked by a monster

indicators.note: revoked is read as re-voked, turned back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A monster cancels someone's student union membership card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student union' reads as one phrase (NUS) but splits: U goes with CARD, reversed to DRACU, then L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula is the vampire of Bram Stoker's novel, a famous monster.

clue.text: WW1's new day welcomes greeting by both sides in turmoil

indicators.note: welcomes means the greeting and the sides are taken in, placed inside the war letters

parts.note: WWI is World War One, with the Roman numeral
hi is a greeting
R and L are right and left, the two sides

explanation.surface: The First World War's new day brings greetings from both sides amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts HIRL inside WWIND, after its first W.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlwind is a scene of frantic confusion, a synonym for turmoil.

clue.text: Leans Against King by the Rolling Stones

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: rolling means tumbling about, so the letters of Stones are rearranged

explanation.surface: A record title: Leans Against by King, credited to the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Rolling Stones' reads as the band; 'Rolling' is the anagram signal for 'Stones'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest on something is to be supported by it, leaning against it.

clue.text: Returning piece earns pieces of gold

indicators.note: returning means the word for piece comes back the other way

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
to earn something is to get it

explanation.surface: A recurring coin earns more coins of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is slang for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuggets are lumps of gold as found in the ground.

clue.text: Caught daughter of Bond's colleague in a slip

indicators.note: caught means heard, as in catching what someone said, so the words are what is spoken

parts.note: Q is the gadget-maker in the James Bond films, and his unmarried daughter would be Miss Q

explanation.surface: Q's daughter from the Bond films is caught out in an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests cricket's C but means overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty shot in snooker or billiards, so a mistake or slip.

clue.text: Expert speller?

parts.note: it suggests a champion at spelling words, but a speller is someone who casts spells

explanation.surface: Someone excellent at spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard or sorcerer is skilled at casting spells, so an expert at spells.

clue.text: Bob's actress

parts.note: the S after the apostrophe in Bob's is used as written
Vivien Leigh, star of Gone with the Wind, is an actress

explanation.surface: Bob's actress: a man's actress, perhaps his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The S comes from the apostrophe-S in "Bob's". 'Bob' is not a name here but a bobsled.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a bobsleigh, a sled for racing down an ice track.

clue.text: Communication with naked ladies, say

indicators.note: say means the result is how it is pronounced, as in for example spoken

parts.note: ladies are females, and naked strips that word of its outer letters, its first and last, leaving EMALE

explanation.surface: A message with pictures of undressed women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' removes the outer letters of FEMALES, and 'say' tells you EMALE is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent over the internet is a form of communication.

clue.text: WW2 planes owned by English captain, it's rumoured?

indicators.note: a rumour is word of mouth, so the phrase is what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: Harry Kane captained the England football team, so something he owns is Harry Kane's

explanation.surface: The England captain is said to own some Second World War aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is an England football captain; 'Harry Kane's' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Portion of cabbage soup may last a while

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A helping of cabbage soup can keep you going for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes ages lasts a long time, a while in the informal sense.

clue.text: Issue of sleeping adults involving open chops

indicators.note: involving means the two As take in the jumbled letters between them

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adults, so two adults give two As

indicators.note: to chop is to cut up, so the letters of open are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown-up complaint about sleeping with one's mouth open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chops' looks like jaws or a mouth, but it is the anagram signal for 'open', whose jumbled letters sit between the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is a pause in breathing during sleep, a sleep disorder.

clue.text: In the past, Germans who overcame England's corners

definitions.text: In the past, Germans who overcame England
definitions.meaning: a Germanic tribe that settled England after the Romans left
corners are points where two lines meet

explanation.surface: Germanic invaders of long ago conquered England's corners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic people who gave England its name, and the geometric term for corners.
